holidays.name: Northern Hemisphere Hoodie-Hoo Day
holidays.description: At noon, step outside, raise your arms, and shout "Hoodie-hoo!" to chase winter away and call in spring. Neighbors may stare. That's part of the fun.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a cheerful, silly ritual for people who are tired of winter.
holidays.funFact: The holiday is specific to the Northern Hemisphere, where late February is when winter fatigue tends to peak.

holidays.name: National Cherry Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the sweet-tart, ruby-red classic with a flaky crust. Eat it warm, with a scoop of vanilla ice cream if you like.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food holiday. It falls in February, a month already linked with cherries through George Washington's birthday and the legend of the cherry tree.
holidays.funFact: Cherry pie is one of the most iconic American desserts. It is also a famous favorite of the TV detective Dale Cooper in the series Twin Peaks.

holidays.name: Love Your Pet Day
holidays.description: A day to give your furry, feathered, or scaly roommate extra treats, cuddles, and playtime. Pets are family, so spoil them a little.
holidays.origin: This is an informal, pet-lover-created observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to appreciate their animal companions and remember the responsibilities of caring for them.
holidays.funFact: Surveys regularly find that most pet owners think of their pets as family members. Many of them buy their pets holiday and birthday gifts.
